newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end up on tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end up on tight liquidity.

text.p: Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds ended higher on Friday as domestic banks remained tight in their liquidity ahead of Monday's deadline for won's reserve requirement, dealers said.
But they expected the yield to start falling next week after the deadline.
* 3-yr corporates closed at 11.70 vs Thursday's 11.57 pct
* 3-mth CDs closed up at 11.65 pct vs 11.60
But dealers expected the yield to start falling by Wednesday as cash flow would be eased after the won reserve requirement.
"Banks and investment trust companies are likely to renew their purchase next week after the deadline," said Kang Yung-gee at Hyundai Securities.
He expected the three-year yield to move between 11.50-80 early in the week.
South Korea's central bank on Friday signed a dollar repurchase agreement (repo) with the People's Bank of China, but dealers said it did not affect the market.
